01UX Engineer · Summer 2026

A summer shipping Tempo’s interface

Tempo is an all-in-one workspace for software teams — issues, docs, design canvas, and code in one place. I spent the summer as a UX engineer designing in production. Everything below shipped to real users.

Role
UX engineering — design + frontend
Timeline
Summer 2026 · 4 months
Team
Design + engineering, all-hands
Tools
Tempo, Tailwind, React

01 — AI Mode

Editing complex code layers directly in the canvas

Although Tempo allows its users to create or edit react pages directly in its canvas, some layers are simply too complex to track their styling. The AI Mode feature I helped ideate allows users to edit complex code layers by stashing their edits as AI prompts while displaying their changes on the canvas. A single click allows the users to seamlessly flow between edits without being interupted by the complexity of the code layer. The AI Mode feature was shipped to production and is now available to all Tempo users.

02 — Design system

Building the design system’s source of truth.

I built Tempo’s design-system canvases; color, elevation, iconography, cursors, every component family from inputs to app-shell templates, rendered from the real production components. Then I made production honor them: shadows onto elevation tokens, off-scale spacing and radii snapped to the published scale, every context menu unified.

03 — Light mode

Giving a dark-first app its second theme.

Tempo was designed dark. I did the light-mode pass across the whole design system; densified the base colour ramp, moved components onto theme-driven tokens, made accent pairs and issue-status colors theme-aware, and wired the preference to persist.

04 — Issues

Redesigning the issues page.

The biggest single body of work: the board, the list, the split view, and everything on an issues card. I also rebuilt the filter system on the design system, added label badges and pickers, and made every card property toggleable.

05 — Everything else

A taste of the 70+ PRs.

  • Micro-motions

    I designed the workspace-creation takeover, gave share pages Shippy, and tuned the tab nav’s microanimations so switching contexts feels physical instead of instant.

  • Share modal, twice
  • Bug report modal

    Rebuilt on the design system; evidence chips, a description that grows before it scrolls, and a confirm before discarding work.

  • Home page

    Colour-coded steps and simple animations to aid a first time user.

  • Changelog

    Redesigned what’s-new modal with accordion releases, reachable from the update toast.

  • Nav previews

    Interactive hover previews on the sidebar glyphs; peek at chats and docs without leaving your location.

06 — Beyond the app

For a complete user experience.

  • Onboarding

    Reorganizing the onboarding flow and redesiging the project kickoff, agent cards, and a merged invite step.

  • Public share pages

    Full redesign of issue, doc, and canvas shares (desktop and mobile) plus the sign-up flow that brings viewers into Tempo.
